definition: The amount you pay to the insurer to keep your cover active, for example every month. You pay it whether or not you get sick.
Something the plan will NOT pay for. If you get treatment for an excluded item, you pay the full cost yourself.
example: Dental care is excluded, so the plan will not pay for a tooth filling.

definition: The time after you join when you cannot claim yet for some services. You still pay premiums during this time.
example: A 10-month waiting period for maternity means you cannot use maternity cover until 10 months after joining.

definition: A small part of the bill that you pay yourself each time you get treatment. The insurer pays the rest.
example: A co-pay of UGX 2,000 per visit: the clinic bill is UGX 20,000, you pay 2,000 and the insurer pays 18,000.

definition: The most the insurer will pay for a type of care in a set time, usually a year. Costs above the limit are yours to pay.
example: Inpatient up to UGX 5M per year: after the insurer has paid UGX 5M that year, you pay any further hospital costs.

definition: Care when you are admitted and stay in hospital, usually overnight or longer.
Care where you visit a clinic or hospital and go home the same day, such as a consultation or lab test.
An illness or health problem you already had before you joined the plan. Many plans do not cover these at first.
A family member, such as a spouse or child, covered under the main member's plan.
Cover for pregnancy check-ups, giving birth and care right after birth.
A clinic or hospital that has an agreement with the insurer. You usually must use these for the plan to pay.
A request to the insurer to pay for treatment you received.
